canonical_question: How does the atomic radius difference between nitrogen (0.75 Å) and oxygen (0.65 Å) specifically quantifiably alter the lattice distortion field to yield exactly 224 MPa higher strength?

question_variants.question: How does the atomic radius difference between nitrogen (0.75 Å) and oxygen (0.65 Å) specifically quantifiably alter the lattice distortion field to yield exactly 224 MPa higher strength?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The paper attributes the 224 MPa strength difference to the larger atomic radius of nitrogen (0.75 Å) compared to oxygen (0.65 Å), which causes higher strengthening. However, the paper does not provide a quantitative calculation or formula linking the specific 0.1 Å difference to the exact 224 MPa yield strength increase; it states the correlation as an inferred conclusion based on the observation.

answers.answer: The paper states that the larger atomic size of nitrogen (0.75 Å) compared to oxygen (0.65 Å) leads to higher strengthening, noting that the yield strength of the N-2 HEA is approximately 224 MPa higher than that of the O-2 HEA. The text asserts this link as an inference supported by the radius comparison but does not provide the specific quantification or equation deriving the 224 MPa value from the atomic size difference.
answers.measurement_outcome: N-2 HEA yield strength ~224 MPa higher than O-2 HEA
answers.mechanism: Higher strengthening due to larger atomic size of nitrogen (0.75 Å) vs oxygen (0.65 Å)
answers.boundary_limitation: No quantitative formula provided linking atomic radius difference to specific MPa value
evidence_spans: For the nitrogen-doped N-2 HEA, an additional low-temperature peak (blue curve) and two high-temperature peaks (green and magenta curves) were also observed (see Fig. 5C ).
The peak height of the additional low-temperature peak is 0.002, and that of the two high-temperature peaks is 0.027 and 0.009, respectively.
Hence, only ~5.3% of all the nitrogen atoms in the N-2 HEA contribute to the formation of ordered nitrogen complexes.
